rv.q: I’d say that “8-Track” probably delivered as much sustenance to the audience as any production in this company’s history, at least based on what I saw happen to people’s faces and breaths.
In fact, “8-Track” is a formidable work of theater - a multifaceted musical portrait of a turbulent period in American history.
This absolutely wonderfully musical revue manages to bring joy to the hearts of every audience member and a smile to their lips.

Whatever it might be missing, though, this play and this company provide an evening of wonderful entertainment as they allow us to travel through our memories to an era that (Viet Nam excluded) seems much more innocent than this one.

If you love, or merely like, the songs of that era (unless seventies for you signifies the birth of punk rock and hip-hop), you're in for a treat with a show that is like one of those old Christmas TV specials with musical numbers only slightly less worn than holiday songs.
8-TRACK: THE SOUNDS OF THE 70'S is a top pick for music lovers of a certain age.
This is a light-weight but entertaining option for people who loved even some of the music of the 70’s or those whose pop music education began in later decades and want a quick primer.

Director-choreographer Jamal Howard’s effervescent and earnest staging of 8-Track brings in queerness (including polyamory), along with shout-outs to feminism (Helen Reddy’s anthemic “I Am Woman” makes an appearance).
Under the directorship of Fred Anzevino has blossomed into a trend setter and probably one of Chicago's finest cabaret theaters.
Theo Ubique is back with verve and fresh talent with 8-TRACK, a sung-through musical built around hit songs from the 1970s...

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically praise "8-Track" as a joyful, high-energy tribute to '70s music, highlighting its powerhouse vocalists, electrifying performances, and ability to get audiences moving with tightly-blended harmonies and nostalgic hits.
